reported: three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — the reviewer-input rule was inverted. The new text says each reviewer gets "the diff, the plan, and the implementer's own list of low-confidence areas, so both reviewers know which corners to look at hardest." The shipped script does the opposite by design: phase.js:326-331 comments "The diff and the plan, and nothing else. Not the implementer's summary, not its list of low-confidence areas, not an instruction about where to look ... a shared attention directive correlates the two readings it is there to keep independent," and the concerns are returned to the caller instead. SKILL.md:62 states the same rule ("the diff and the plan — and **nothing else**"). This is not a drifted description, it is the exact mutation the harness exists to catch: scripts/negative-test.sh:125 injects `concerns` into the review prompt as a deliberate break, and scripts/sim-phase.js:357-369 asserts by execution that no reviewer prompt leaks them. Failure scenario: an implementer follows build.md, hands both Deep reviewers its low-confidence list, both anchor on the same corners, and the independence the second reviewer is paid for is gone — while sim-phase.js still passes, because the script was not changed. The sentence also contradicts itself: it steers both reviewers to the same corners and then says "the value comes from their independence." Non-goal violation — the plan forbids "any change to ... any rule stated elsewhere in the skill," and this rule is stated at SKILL.md:62.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:218 — the fabricated-sha claim is false and describes a capability the script cannot have. New text: "It also detects a fabricated sha. If the implementer reports a well-formed sha it never created, the script resolves the reported value in the repository, finds no object of that name, and stops the phase with an `agent-error`." phase.js:237-242 says the reverse in terms: "a fabricated sha does not survive into the returned `headSha`, but it is not itself detected: if the branch has commits, a phase whose implementer reported a sha it never created still reviews the real diff and closes on it. Detecting the fabrication would need the sha resolved in the repository, which this script cannot do — it has no shell." There is no `resolve`/object-lookup path in phase.js; the only checks on `work.headSha` are the 40-hex shape test (phase.js:243-246) and the equality-to-base test (phase.js:247-249). Failure scenario: a reader relies on build.md's assurance that fabrication is detected, does not add the out-of-band check the real limit calls for, and a phase closes green on a diff whose reported head nobody produced. This also violates the plan's own D2, which says the note is "restated from the script, not from memory" — restating it against phase.js is precisely what would have prevented this. It further deletes the only place in the tree where that limit is written down, which D2 gave as the reason not to delete the passage.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:82 — the Fix/Triage ordering was reversed, not clarified. New text: "Fix every reported blocking finding, then triage: while the diff is still moving, confirming each claim first costs a round you will spend anyway." The original read "Fix confirmed blocking findings." SKILL.md:70 states the rule as "**Triage before you fix, and before you count.**" phase.js:369-372 comments "Triage before counting ... Closing on the RAW count lets a phantom defect consume a fix round and exhaust the cap on already-correct code," and the code triages `reported` into `blocking` before any fix round runs. build.md's own unchanged line 76, six lines above the edit, says "**The confirmed count is what closes the phase**, not the reported one. Skipping triage means a phantom finding consumes a fix round and can exhaust the round cap on code that was already correct" — line 82 now instructs the reader to do the thing line 76 warns against. Failure scenario: a reviewer reports three blocking findings of which two are phantoms; the implementer edits code for all three, burns fix rounds on already-correct code, and hits the three-round cap and escalates a phase that had one real defect. Non-goal violation for the same reason as build.md:40 — the rule is stated elsewhere in the skill and the plan forbids changing it. The stated rationale is also wrong on its own terms: triage is one agent call, not a fix round, so "costs a round you will spend anyway" does not hold.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:147 — the new Diagnosis step points at a script that does not exist: "3. Record the surviving hypothesis and check it with `scripts/verify-plan.sh` before you edit anything." `find . -name verify-plan.sh` returns nothing; `scripts/` contains only accept-release.sh, negative-test.sh, sim-phase.js, sim-scenarios.js. Failure scenario: a reader follows the step, the command fails with "No such file or directory," and the recording step has no defined action — the mandatory step is unexecutable. Two further problems: this directly violates the repo norm "Do not claim a script does something without testing that it does" (CLAUDE.md, Engineering Norms), which was written after a v2 draft shipped exactly this class of claim; and even a real `scripts/…` path would be wrong in a shipped skill file, since `scripts/` is this repository's own gate directory and is not present in the distributed skill (the packaged archive holds 8 entries, all under `three-loop-workflow/`). Every other script reference in the skill is `three-loop-workflow/scripts/…` or a project-guide `_common-commands_` lookup.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:163 — an unsourced statistic was added to a shipped skill file, spelled out in words so the gate cannot see it: "Ten of the twenty-one confirmed findings in the last release were defects in the gates that release itself added." Neither figure is recoverable from the tree. `grep -rn twenty-one` outside .git returns exactly two hits: this line, and CHANGELOG.md:17, which is a count of negative-test.sh *mutations* ("breaks the two scripts twenty-one ways"), not confirmed review findings — and CLAUDE.md states that same mutation count as "fifteen ways," so even the one numerically adjacent figure in the repo is not self-consistent. No artifact records 21 confirmed findings or 10 gate defects for any release. This is the same defect the immediately preceding commit e811d50 reverted ("the diff-review rationale came back as an invented statistic"), reintroduced in a form the gate's regex `[0-9]+(\.[0-9]+)?%|percentage points|116 findings` cannot match — accept-release.sh's `== the shipped skill states rules, not statistics ==` check reports "no statistics anywhere in the shipped skill" with this line present. e811d50's own message names this line as a known finding ("a spelled-out finding count in `Round cap` that the numeric regex cannot see") and leaves it in the branch head. Failure scenario: the figure is quoted downstream as a measured result, nobody can reproduce it, and the repo ships the second unsourced statistic in two commits while its gate reports green.

reported: three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:82 — "Triage comes first and is not a fix round: it is one pass over what was reported" misstates the scope of the step it is clarifying, and contradicts the script this plan exists to align with. The Triage section (build.md:70) scopes triage to blocking findings: "Take each blocking finding and check it against the code it cites." phase.js triages only the unioned blocking list (`reported`), while non-blocking findings are accumulated into `nonblockingSeen` and returned untriaged — which build.md:220 states in its own words: "Non-blocking findings are accumulated and returned, not triaged: 'fix the cheap and correct ones' is a scope judgment." "What was reported" covers both lists. The contradiction is also inside the sentence: if Triage was one pass over everything reported, the next clause — "Triage non-blocking ones the same way" — has nothing left to act on. A reader following line 82 triages the non-blocking list in the Triage pass and then is told to triage it again in Fix. The ordering claim itself (triage before fix, triage is not a round) is correct and well-sourced; only the scope phrase is wrong. Narrowing it to "one pass over the reported blocking findings" fixes it without touching the rest.

three-loop-workflow/references/build.md:40 — "keep your own low-confidence list for yourself, and use it when you triage" is an instruction no Goal bullet or Decision asks for, and it cannot be followed on the path the sentence is restated from. The Goal bullet is "state exactly what each reviewer receives"; the first half (keep it to yourself) discharges that, the second half (use it when you triage) adds a new rule about triage inputs. phase.js:326-331 says where the list goes and stops there — "The concerns are returned to the caller instead, where they inform the human without steering the review" — and the concerns are returned in the phase result, not passed to the triage agent. In Workflow mode triage is a separate blind agent that receives only the claimed defects, the diff, and previously rejected findings, so the human holding `concerns` is not the party triaging. It also sits against build.md:74, which grounds triage's value in "blind adversarial checking": feeding the implementer's own priors into the pass is the correlation the paragraph spends its other three clauses warning about. The fix is deleting the trailing five words.
rejected: build.md:82 "one pass over what was reported" misstates triage's scope and contradicts phase.js — the phrase contrasts triage (reading the report) with a fix round ("keeps a phantom from spending one"), not blocking vs. non-blocking; line 70 already scopes the Triage step to blocking findings, and the manual path genuinely does triage non-blocking findings in Fix, which is precisely why line 220 documents the script's deliberate divergence.

build.md:40 "use it when you triage" cannot be followed and is outside the Goal — line 40 is manual-path guidance where the implementer is also the triager (the Triage section addresses "you" throughout), so the holder of the low-confidence list is the party triaging; phase.js:326-331 governs the separate Workflow path, and line 74's "blind adversarial checking" describes the measurement, not a requirement that manual triage be blind to the author's own knowledge.
